name: Rank-Preserving Downset Filtering
statement: If nonempty $C$ is downward closed in $U$ and $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^U$ is a nonempty downset, then $F=C|_D$ is nonempty and $\operatorname{Sh}(F)=\{T\in\operatorname{Sh}(C):T\cap U\in D\}$. Ampleness is preserved. If $C$ has a rank-$r$ parent with $m$ auxiliaries, then $F$ has one of rank $r$ with at most $m+\sum_{J\in\mathcal N(D)}\max(0,r+1-|J|)$ auxiliaries; in particular the least parent rank cannot increase.
proof: Downward closure identifies the section at the characteristic word of $B\subseteq U$ with the private shattering data over $B$, giving the exact support formula and, by counting ample sections, ampleness. Standardize the supplied parent in all constrained coordinates so every minimal forbidden support of $D$ becomes a compatible all-one minimum section. Compatible minimum-section deletion removes those patterns while retaining the old mark, rank, and stated auxiliary bound.
